Offering Vermont plus $250 cash is also unworkable. p4 would receive only a singleton light blue property, and p2 already holds Connecticut. That would let p2 trade with p4 and break my light blue block.

I will keep Vermont to block p2's light blue set. I am not going to trade it away.

I confirmed that completing any color set for p4 is impossible this turn. Their condition cannot be met, and a higher cash offer would still be rejected.

I am weighing whether to raise the offer to $350 or end the turn and wait. Trading uses an action and may signal desperation, so I will not open higher than $350. I am also considering offering a utility for New York Avenue, but splitting my only income source would reduce rent from 10x dice to 4x.

I cannot afford to build houses on the orange monopoly even with a $350 bid, so I would own the set without any houses until I raise cash. Utility income averages about $70 per hit, which is steady but modest. Since p4 explicitly rejected cash-only offers, raising the bid further would likely just signal desperation and invite another rejection.

I rejected a creative offer to give p4 Indiana and Vermont, because that would arm other players without completing their color set. I also considered trading with p2 for Pacific and Ventnor, but I lack the cash and those properties do not complete sets for me. Keeping Indiana is now a second win path. If I land on Kentucky, I would own two of three red streets and could then trade for Illinois from p3. I will not sell Indiana or Vermont; they are future monopoly pieces. The utilities remain mine.

I am now considering p3 for Illinois. They hold the rail monopoly and that red street.

I will not spend $400 on a railroad. That would leave me with only $140 and no orange set. p3 now has $1055, so they are even less likely to sell a rail. I am considering one more structured offer to p4 that is not pure cash. I might trade with p2 first to acquire a property they need, then trade with p4.

The engine allows sequential trades within a single turn. I can trade with p2 first to acquire Ventnor or Pacific, then trade those properties to p4. However, even with those pieces, p4 still needs bank-owned properties—Atlantic for yellow and Pennsylvania for green—to complete their color sets.

I realized that giving p4 both St. James and Tennessee would complete their orange set, but that would destroy my own orange monopoly. I also considered trading both orange properties plus cash for scattered properties like Boardwalk and Marvin, but that would leave me with scattered pieces and give p4 the only buildable color set.

I will end the turn. Liquid cash is safer than bidding against myself for New York Avenue. I need to survive upcoming railroad hits and be ready to buy unowned properties like Kentucky or Virginia.

I will not mortgage. I will end the turn and tell p4 that no color set is fully finished yet, so New York Avenue stays the only immediate target. I will not raise the offer.
